newsitem.title: USA: Charges against father in Danish baby case dropped.
newsitem.headline: Charges against father in Danish baby case dropped.

text.p: A New York judge on Wednesday dropped criminal charges against a Danish infant's American father who was accused of leaving the child outside a restaurant during a meal.

Authorities alleged that playwright Exavier Wardlaw, 49, and the infant's mother, Danish actress Annette Sorensen, had left the baby outside while they had a drink and watched her through a window last month.
Passersby noticed 14-month-old Liv was crying and they called police.
Wardlaw was charged with endangering the welfare of a child and disorderly conduct.
The case sparked a transatlantic debate after Sorensen was charged and jailed for two days. The baby was placed in foster care for four days in what her lawyer called a "clash of cultures."
Sorensen returned to Copenhagen after the charges were dropped. She told reporters there she deserved an apology from New York City officials.
"This is the stroller-tot episode that brought New York City to the brink of war with Denmark," Ron Kuby, Wardlaw's lawyer, told Manhattan Criminal Court Judge Donna Recant.
The judge and a New York prosecutor agreed without any arguments to dismiss the case.

Under the terms of the plea bargain agreeement, Wardlaw has not admitted guilt and a record of the charges will be sealed if he remains out of trouble for six months. Wardlaw was accompanied to court by his eldest daughter. He and Sorensen are not married.
Kuby said he was considering filing a federal civil rights action against the police. He alleged that when Wardlaw was arrested he was "kicked" and "his head shoved in a toilet at the precinct."
Sorensen had been in the United States less than 48 hours when the incident occurred.
